title: Status and Error Technical Reference
readerIntent: Audit status identity, propagation, response safety, and observability.
priorKnowledge: Read the status and error journey.
owner: Owning capability and Nodics status/error contracts
summary: Every outcome has stable identity, owner, classification, safe message intent, propagation rules, diagnostics, and tests.

sections.heading: Status authority
items: Each owning module defines stable success and error codes in its status catalog. Response handlers resolve registered codes and must not invent an unregistered success code at runtime.
Codes are machine contracts; user-facing messages are safe, localizable content. HTTP response status, Nodics code, name, context, and trace identity serve different purposes.
Callers branch on documented code or category rather than parsing English text or stack output.

sections.heading: Error creation and propagation
items: Create errors at the boundary that understands the failure, preserve the causal chain, add safe structured context, and allow shared handlers to map the response.
Do not repeatedly wrap the same error, overwrite its code, expose provider internals, or convert authorization denial into a generic success.
Pipelines record the failing layer and phase once while correlation connects downstream calls and asynchronous work.

sections.heading: Response and security
items: Public responses omit credentials, tokens, personal data, filesystem paths, stacks, queries, provider payloads, and policy details useful for enumeration.
Authentication failures remain intentionally generic; protected logs may distinguish safe outcome categories without recording submitted secrets.
Validation errors identify permitted fields and constraints while respecting field masking and tenant boundaries.

sections.heading: Customization and compatibility
items: Custom modules allocate codes within their owned catalog, document semantics and HTTP mapping, and register them through existing status loading contracts.
Do not copy another module's code for a different meaning or place application status configuration in package.json.
Changing established semantics is a contract change requiring compatibility, consumers, documentation, migration, and regression review.

sections.heading: Verification and operations
items: Test every code registration, success mapping, validation aggregation, causal chain, unknown-code failure, localization, masking, and API contract.
Monitor bounded error categories and rates with trace correlation; never use raw messages or user identifiers as metric labels.
Troubleshooting starts with response code and trace identity, then follows safe module, pipeline, provider, and audit evidence to the authority.

sections.heading: Checklist
items: Unique stable code, capability owner, success/error classification, and response category.
Safe default message and separate presentation/localization key where needed.
Allowed contexts, cause preservation, trace identity, and cross-module mapping.
Public allowlist and protected diagnostic fields.
Logs, metrics, alerting, audit, retention, and privacy.
Positive, negative, unknown-code, boundary, contract, integration, security-redaction, trace, and regression tests.
